caption: The drawing depicts a cylindrical, two-handled stoneware jar or crock positioned upright against a plain, light-colored background. The object is grayish-blue in overall hue with prominent cobalt blue decorative elements. There are two looped handles, one on each side near the top. The central portion of the vessel is inscribed in large, uppercase, stenciled blue lettering with the words: "MANUFACTURED BY J.H. MILLER BRANDENBURG, KY." Surrounding the text on both the upper and lower portions of the crock are stylized blue floral and foliate patterns, including leafy branches and dot motifs. The shadows and gradients suggest the cylindrical form and volume of the jar, and the handles are rendered in a lighter, grayish-tan color. The drawing occupies the center of the paper, with a handwritten note and number at the bottom in red ink, and the name "Edward Wilehanice" lightly written in pencil near the base of the crock.
title: Stoneware Jar
